section_summary: This section documents the operations, logistics, budgeting, and personnel clearance for the project microfilming Japanese Foreign Office archives in Tokyo under Glenn W. Shaw and Thomas C. Smith, funded by the Library of Congress and supported by SCAP. It also details Department of State efforts to locate and distribute microfilm copies of the former Japanese Embassy archives in Brussels through the 7707th Military Intelligence Service Center to satisfy quadripartite custodial obligations. Finally, the records cover inter-agency policy agreements establishing that pre-December 7, 1941 Japanese microfilms deposited in the Library of Congress would be made available without restriction to researchers and institutions, including the Hoover Institute.

subfiles.about: Shaw requests an allotment of one hundred dollars for incidental expenses for the diplomatic documents project in Tokyo.
subfiles.from: Tokyo (Cloyce K. Huston / Glenn W. Shaw)
subfiles.summary: Shaw requests a one-hundred-dollar allotment to USPOLAD for incidental expenses of the diplomatic documents project.
subfiles.title: Telegram 145 from Tokyo Requesting Incidental Expense Allotment
subfiles.to: Secretary of State (for G. Bernard Noble)

subfiles.about: Authorizes an expenditure not to exceed one hundred dollars for incidental supplies for the Japanese War Documents Project.
subfiles.from: Department of State (Dean Acheson / G. Bernard Noble)
subfiles.summary: The Department authorizes an expenditure up to one hundred dollars against a State trust fund for Japanese documents project supplies.
subfiles.title: Telegram 211 to Tokyo Authorizing Incidental Expenditure
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo (for Glenn W. Shaw)

subfiles.about: Designates the attached copy of Tokyo telegram 167 as the official record copy to replace the missing original action copy.
subfiles.from: Department of State Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.summary: Department Form M-184 designating the attached copy of Tokyo telegram 167 as the replacement record copy.
subfiles.title: Replacement Record Sheet for Tokyo Telegram 167
subfiles.to: Central Records

subfiles.about: Inquires by radio whether the working fund appropriation for the documents project falls under the Special Army Appropriation.
subfiles.from: Tokyo (Cloyce K. Huston)
subfiles.summary: Huston in Tokyo asks whether appropriation 19X8300.003 for the documents project is administered under SAA.
subfiles.title: Telegram 167 from Tokyo regarding SAA Status of Appropriation
subfiles.to: Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Informs the Acting Political Adviser in Tokyo that appropriation 19X8300.003 is not under the Special Army Appropriation.
subfiles.from: Department of State (James E. Webb / G. Bernard Noble)
subfiles.summary: Noble informs Huston that appropriation 19X8300.003 is not under SAA.
subfiles.title: Telegram to Tokyo Clarifying SAA Status of Appropriation
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo (for Cloyce K. Huston)

subfiles.about: Requests clearance for the wives of Glenn W. Shaw and Thomas C. Smith to travel to Japan by commercial transportation.
subfiles.from: Department of State (James E. Webb / G. Bernard Noble)
subfiles.summary: The Department requests entry clearance for the wives of Glenn W. Shaw and Thomas C. Smith to travel to Japan.
subfiles.title: Telegram to Tokyo Requesting Travel Clearance for Spouses
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo (for Cloyce K. Huston)

subfiles.about: Designates the attached copy of Tokyo telegram 192 as the official record copy to replace the unreturned action copy.
subfiles.from: Department of State Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.summary: Form M-184 designating the attached copy of Tokyo telegram 192 as the permanent record copy.
subfiles.title: Replacement Record Sheet for Tokyo Telegram 192
subfiles.to: Central Records

subfiles.about: Reports that entry applications for the wives of Shaw and Smith have been submitted to Army Headquarters on a priority list.
subfiles.from: Tokyo (Cloyce K. Huston)
subfiles.summary: Huston reports that entry applications for Shaw's and Smith's wives were placed on the Army priority list for travel after mid-September.
subfiles.title: Telegram 192 from Tokyo regarding Travel Clearance for Spouses
subfiles.to: Secretary of State (pass to G. Bernard Noble)

subfiles.about: Shaw requests an additional shipment of microfilm to Tokyo via the diplomatic pouch.
subfiles.from: Tokyo (Cloyce K. Huston / Glenn W. Shaw)
subfiles.summary: Shaw requests that the Department ship more microfilm to Tokyo via pouch.
subfiles.title: Telegram 211 from Tokyo Requesting Additional Microfilm
subfiles.to: Secretary of State (for G. Bernard Noble)

subfiles.about: Advises Shaw that eighty rolls of microfilm were sent by air pouch and 960 rolls shipped via S.S. Mansfield.
subfiles.from: Department of State (James E. Webb / G. Bernard Noble)
subfiles.summary: Noble informs Shaw that eighty rolls of film were dispatched by air pouch and 960 rolls via sea to Yokohama.
subfiles.title: Telegram to Tokyo regarding Microfilm Shipments
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo (for Glenn W. Shaw)

subfiles.about: Designates the attached copy of Tokyo telegram 256 as the official record copy to replace the unreturned action copy.
subfiles.from: Department of State Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.summary: Form M-184 designating the attached copy of Tokyo telegram 256 as the replacement record copy.
subfiles.title: Replacement Record Sheet for Tokyo Telegram 256
subfiles.to: Central Records

subfiles.about: Shaw requests the airmail shipment of one dozen field indicator light bulbs for microfilming equipment.
subfiles.from: Tokyo (Cloyce K. Huston / Glenn W. Shaw)
subfiles.summary: Shaw requests one dozen field indicator light bulbs for microfilming equipment sent to Tokyo by airmail.
subfiles.title: Telegram 256 from Tokyo Requesting Field Indicator Bulbs
subfiles.to: Secretary of State (for G. Bernard Noble)

subfiles.about: Transmits Despatch 389 from Brussels and requests procurement of five microfilm sets of the Japanese Embassy archives from the 7707th MISC.
subfiles.from: Department of State (Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State instructs the High Commissioner to request five microfilm sets of the Brussels Japanese Embassy archives from the 7707th MISC.
subfiles.title: Instruction 265 to Berlin regarding Brussels Embassy Archives Microfilm
subfiles.to: United States High Commissioner for Germany, Berlin

subfiles.about: Requests four sets of microfilm copies of the former Japanese Embassy archives to fulfill custodial commitments to the Russian, British, and Chinese embassies.
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Brussels (G. J. Heyneker)
subfiles.summary: The Brussels Embassy requests four microfilm sets of former Japanese Embassy archives filmed in 1947 by the 7707th MISC for joint custodians.
subfiles.title: Despatch 389 from Brussels regarding Japanese Embassy Archives (Action Copy)
subfiles.to: Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Reports that searches with Army Intelligence, German Military Documents, and CIA found no trace of the Brussels Japanese archives, suggesting referral to POLAD Germany.
subfiles.from: Edward J. Carroll (Division of Protective Services, IAD)
subfiles.summary: Carroll reports that checks with Army Intelligence and CIA yielded no trace of the Brussels archives and recommends consulting POLAD Germany.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Search for Brussels Japanese Embassy Archives
subfiles.to: Mr. Chappell (Division of Protective Services, DS)

subfiles.about: Designates the attached copy of Brussels despatch 389 as the official record copy to replace the unreturned action copy.
subfiles.from: Department of State Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.summary: Form M-184 designating the attached copy of Brussels despatch 389 as the permanent replacement record copy.
subfiles.title: Replacement Record Sheet for Brussels Despatch 389
subfiles.to: Central Records

subfiles.about: Control copy of Despatch 389 requesting four sets of microfilm copies of former Japanese Embassy archives in Brussels for distribution to joint custodians.
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Brussels (G. J. Heyneker)
subfiles.summary: Control copy of Brussels despatch 389 requesting four sets of microfilms of former Japanese Embassy archives to fulfill custodial promises.
subfiles.title: Despatch 389 from Brussels regarding Japanese Embassy Archives (Control Copy)
subfiles.to: Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Reviews the progress of the Japanese Foreign Office microfilming project in Tokyo and requests an additional working fund transfer of $22,087.25.
subfiles.from: G. Bernard Noble (Chief, Division of Historical Policy Research, for the Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Noble summarizes the progress and budget of the Tokyo microfilming project, requesting an additional $22,087.25 from the Library of Congress to complete the filming through fiscal year 1951.
subfiles.title: Letter to Librarian of Congress Requesting Additional Funds for Japanese Documents Program
subfiles.to: Luther H. Evans (Librarian of Congress)

subfiles.about: Recommends that Japanese Foreign Office microfilms deposited in the Library of Congress be made available without restrictions down to December 7, 1941.
subfiles.from: G. Bernard Noble (Chief, Division of Historical Policy Research)
subfiles.summary: Noble recommends making Japanese Foreign Office microfilms transferred to the Library of Congress unrestricted for scholars down to December 7, 1941, reviewing later materials subsequently.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Recommending Unrestricted Access to Pre-War Japanese Microfilms
subfiles.to: John M. Allison (FE), Gerald Swihart (PA), Howland H. Sargeant (P), Dean Rusk (G)

subfiles.about: Concurs in making Japanese Foreign Office microfilms through December 7, 1941 unrestricted to responsible parties and suggests initiating review of war-period films.
subfiles.from: John M. Allison (Director, Office of Northeast Asian Affairs, FE)
subfiles.summary: Allison concurs in releasing microfilms through December 7, 1941 without restrictions to all responsible parties and suggests reviewing war-period films for declassification.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Concurring in Clearance of Pre-War Japanese Microfilms
subfiles.to: G. Bernard Noble (Chief, Division of Historical Policy Research, RE)

subfiles.about: Confirms after speaking with John Andreassen that the Library of Congress will make unrestricted microfilms available without discrimination, including to foreign governments.
subfiles.from: G. Bernard Noble (Chief, Division of Historical Policy Research, RE)
subfiles.summary: Noble reports that Andreassen confirmed the Library of Congress will provide unrestricted pre-war microfilms to all responsible parties without discrimination.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Library of Congress Policy on Japanese Records Microfilms
subfiles.to: Alice L. Dunning (Division of Northeast Asian Affairs, NA)

subfiles.about: Transmits one set of microfilms of the former Japanese Embassy in Brussels to the Department and confirms four sets were sent to Embassy Brussels.
subfiles.from: Acting Political Adviser to the United States High Commissioner for Germany, Frankfurt (John A. Calhoun)
subfiles.summary: Calhoun transmits one set of Brussels Japanese Embassy microfilms to the Department and notes four copies were forwarded directly to Brussels.
subfiles.title: Despatch 804 from Frankfurt Transmitting Brussels Embassy Microfilms
subfiles.to: Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Inquires informally whether the Hoover Institute could obtain a complete set of the Japanese Foreign Office microfilms being produced in Tokyo.
subfiles.from: C. Easton Rothwell (Vice-Chairman, Hoover Institute and Library, Stanford University)
subfiles.summary: Rothwell inquires whether the Hoover Institute can acquire a complete set of the Japanese Foreign Office microfilms, citing curator Nobutaka Ike and Thomas C. Smith's involvement.
subfiles.title: Letter from Hoover Institute Inquiring about Japanese Microfilm Collection
subfiles.to: Francis H. Russell (Director, Office of Public Affairs)

subfiles.about: Explains that Japanese microfilms are deposited in the Library of Congress for duplication and distribution to research institutions, advising future contact.
subfiles.from: Francis H. Russell (Director, Office of Public Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Russell explains that Japanese Foreign Office microfilms are deposited with the Library of Congress for distribution and recommends contacting them once accessioning progresses.
subfiles.title: Letter to Hoover Institute regarding Distribution of Japanese Microfilms
subfiles.to: C. Easton Rothwell (Vice-Chairman, Hoover Institute and Library)

subfiles.about: Recounts the project's background from a 1947 publication proposal to the 1949 microfilming project funded by the Library of Congress.
subfiles.from: Richard A. Humphrey (Assistant Chief, Division of Historical Policy Research, RE)
subfiles.summary: Humphrey outlines the evolution of the project from a 1947 publication plan into a Library of Congress-funded microfilming operation begun in April 1949.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Reviewing History of Japanese Records Microfilm Project
subfiles.to: Harold W. Mosely (Division of Northeast Asian Affairs, NA)

subfiles.about: Requests an urgent reply from Shaw regarding adequate identification of contents on the Japanese Foreign Office microfilm rolls.
subfiles.from: Department of State (James E. Webb / G. Bernard Noble)
subfiles.summary: Noble urges Shaw to reply promptly regarding the adequate identification of the contents on the Japanese microfilm rolls.
subfiles.title: Telegram to Tokyo Inquiring about Identification of Microfilm Contents
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo (for Glenn W. Shaw)
